logistics.title: Plan for the week
logistics.text: Go after the big group leaves: fly to Samui on Mon 18 Jan if they leave that morning, or on Tue 19. Mon 18: Chill Up and maybe a Seaside pre-Full Moon party. Tue 19: OXA or the Lighthouse. Wed 20: Waterfall. Thu 21: Jungle Experience. Fri 22: the Full Moon Party. Sat 23: boat to Samui and the 15:05 flight back to Phuket for Circoloco.

logistics.title: Fastest way: fly Phuket to Koh Samui, then a boat
logistics.text: Bangkok Airways is the only nonstop airline from Phuket (HKT) to Koh Samui (USM). On Mon 18 and Tue 19 Jan 2027 there are 8 flights a day, 55 minutes: 07:30, 09:45, 11:00, 12:55, 14:15, 16:35, 17:30 and 19:55, from about 4,730 THB one way (Google Flights, 16 Oct 2026). Take the 14:15 flight or earlier. Later flights miss the last boats to Thong Sala; only the Haad Rin Queen speedboat at 18:30 still goes to Haad Rin.

logistics.title: Samui airport to Koh Phangan in one ticket
logistics.text: Lomprayah sells airport-to-Phangan tickets with the van to Bangrak pier included: about every hour from 07:30 to 15:00 and a last one at 17:00, 500 THB, about 1 hour to Thong Sala pier (700 THB with a drop at your hotel; 2026 timetable). Seatran Discovery has airport departures at 07:30, 09:00, 12:00 and 14:00 on 18-19 Jan 2027, also 500 THB (670 THB to your hotel).

logistics.title: Pier to pier: Samui to Koh Phangan
logistics.text: From Bangrak pier (near the airport) Lomprayah boats leave about every hour from 08:00 to 17:30, 350 THB, 30 minutes to Thong Sala; Seatran leaves at 08:00, 09:30, 12:30 and 14:30 (350 THB). The Haad Rin Queen goes from Bangrak straight to Haad Rin: ferry 10:30 and 17:00 (200 THB, 50 min), speedboat 15:00 and 18:30 (500 THB, 25 min).

logistics.title: Bus + boat from Phuket in one ticket (slow but cheap)
logistics.text: Lomprayah picks you up in Patong, Kata, Karon, Rawai or Nai Harn at 07:30, or at Phuket airport (gate 1-2) at 10:00, and you reach Koh Phangan at 16:30 by bus and catamaran: 1,600 THB, or 1,800 THB with a drop at your hotel. From its Phuket Town office it leaves at 09:30 for 1,400 THB. Kamala is not in the pickup zone. Cheaper bus + ferry tickets via Surat Thani (Phantip, Raja Ferry and others) cost about 600-900 THB and take most of the day.

logistics.title: Raja car ferry (only with a car or a bus ticket)
logistics.text: Raja Ferry crosses from Donsak on the mainland to Thong Sala at 05:00, 08:00, 11:00, 14:00 and 18:00 (2 h 30 min), and from Lipa Noi on Samui in about 1 h 30 min. It is slow; you only use it on a bus + ferry ticket or with a car.

logistics.title: Back to Phuket on Sat 23 Jan for Circoloco
logistics.text: Samui to Phuket flights on Sat 23 Jan 2027: 08:15, 09:20, 11:10, 15:05, 15:50, 18:15 and 19:00 (1 hour, about 4,900 THB on 16 Oct 2026). The realistic plan after the Full Moon night: a 10:30 or 11:00 Seatran boat (or the 10:45 Lomprayah) from Thong Sala to Bangrak, then the 15:05 flight; you land at 16:05 and reach Baba Beach Club Natai (about 30 min) around 17:00. Circoloco runs 15:00-03:00. Book this flight now: there are only 7 a day.

logistics.title: Earliest boats from Koh Phangan on Sat 23 Jan
logistics.text: From Thong Sala the first boat is the Lomprayah speedboat at 07:30 to Bangrak (arrives 08:00, 350 THB; 2026 timetable). With its van ticket (500 THB) you are at Samui airport at 08:30, in time for the 09:20 flight. Later: Seatran 10:30 and 11:00 (500 THB with the airport transfer, at the airport 12:00 or 12:30). From Haad Rin: Haad Rin Queen ferry 09:30 (200 THB) or speedboat 12:30 (500 THB) to Bangrak.

logistics.title: Backup if the flights are full
logistics.text: The Lomprayah bus + boat leaves Thong Sala at 11:00 and reaches its Phuket Town office at 18:30 (1,400 THB, 2026 timetable). Other bus + ferry tickets to Phuket Bus Terminal 2 leave in the morning and take 10-12 hours; check 12Go for times. From Phuket Town it is about 1 hour by taxi north to Natai.

logistics.title: Full Moon week: rooms cost more, book now
logistics.text: In party week rooms near Haad Rin cost about 2-3 times the normal price, and many places ask for a 3-5 night minimum stay. Haad Rin sells out weeks before, and January is also peak season. Book in October or November. Ban Tai and Thong Sala are much cheaper bases.

logistics.title: Where to stay: Ban Tai is the best base
logistics.text: Most parties this week are in the Ban Tai hills or on its beach: OXA, Jungle Experience, Waterfall, Retro Mountain, Unclave, Chill Up and Sabaii. Haad Rin (Full Moon, Lighthouse, taxi boats to Eden) is 10-20 minutes away by taxi, and Thong Sala pier about 10 minutes. Stay in Haad Rin only if you want to walk home from the Full Moon Party and accept the minimum stay.

logistics.title: Getting around at night
logistics.text: Shared taxis (pickup trucks, called songthaew) run late between Thong Sala, Ban Tai and Haad Rin on party nights. They have no meter, so agree the price per person before you get in. A guide gives about 200 THB per person from Thong Sala to Haad Rin. For Eden Garden and Bambu take a 4x4 truck from the Ban Tai 7-Eleven or a taxi boat from Haad Rin.

logistics.title: Scooters: better not at night
logistics.text: Thai law requires a helmet. Many rental scooters are not registered for the road, and without a licence that covers motorbikes your travel insurance may not pay (UK travel advice). A scooter rental blog says the steep Haad Rin hill and riding home after drinking are the two biggest causes of scooter accidents on Koh Phangan. On party nights take a taxi.

links.label: Scooter to the Full Moon Party (Byklo, 2026)

logistics.title: Full Moon Party safety
logistics.text: Buy your own bucket and watch it being mixed: drinks are strong, spiking happens, and drinks with methanol can kill (UK travel advice). Stay away from the fire rope and fire limbo, and do not swim at night. Leave passport and cards in the room safe, carry a photo of your passport and small cash, and agree a meeting point with your friend.

logistics.title: Drugs, vapes and police
logistics.text: Even small amounts of drugs can mean heavy fines or prison, and police are active on party nights. Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal in Thailand: fines are usually 5,000-30,000 THB, with no exception for tourists. In an emergency call the Tourist Police on 1155.

logistics.title: What to bring
logistics.text: Cash: the Full Moon entry (200 THB), the taxis, and OXA and the Hollystone bar take cash only. ATMs in Haad Rin can run out around the full moon, and each withdrawal costs 250-350 THB. Bring closed shoes (broken glass on the sand), clothes you do not mind ruining with UV paint, a waterproof phone pouch, a small torch for the paths to Eden and Lighthouse, a power bank, and your passport or ID (Jungle Experience and Hollystone are 20+).

logistics.title: Find each week's parties
logistics.text: Most January line-ups and small parties are posted only 1-2 weeks before. Check the phangan.events calendar and the Phangan Party Guide channel on Telegram, which posts the parties of each day.

logistics.title: If you stay longer on Koh Phangan
logistics.text: If you skip Circoloco: Eden Garden and Hollystone (Sat 23), Waterfall, Bambu and a WET pool party (Sun 24). Fly back to Phuket on Mon 25 Jan (Samui flights from 08:15 to 19:00). Do not leave it for Tue 26: a late boat or a delayed Samui flight could make you miss the 18:20 flight home.

departure.title: Be at the airport by 15:20
departure.text: For the 18:20 flight, arrive about 3 hours before, by 15:20. Late January is high season, and the lines at check-in, security and passport control can be long. Most airlines close check-in 40-60 minutes before take-off, so check the time on your ticket.

departure.title: When to leave for the airport
departure.text: Leave Nai Yang by 15:00 (5-10 min), Kamala by 14:15 (40-60 min), Patong by 13:45 (50-90 min) and Kata by 13:15 (60-100 min). Traffic going north gets bad after 16:00, and heavy rain makes it slower.

links.label: Drive times and rush hour (Phuket 101, Mar 2026)

departure.title: Book the ride the day before
departure.text: In Grab, use 'Advance Booking'. You can book from 90 days to 75 minutes before pickup. The price is fixed and includes a booking fee of about 50-100 baht. Bolt also lets you book up to 90 days ahead. If your hotel books a car, agree the price first.

departure.title: Cheapest ride: the Smart Bus
departure.text: Smart Bus Route 1 runs along the west coast to the airport for 100 baht. To arrive at about 14:50, take it at Kata Palm 12:47, Patong (Bangla police box) 13:20 or Kamala Big C 13:35. The bus before (12:12, 12:50, 13:05) arrives about 14:20 and is safer with traffic. Timetable from 16 Jan 2026: check it again before you go.

departure.title: Check-out is at 11:00 or 12:00
departure.text: Most hotels near the airport want you out by 12:00. Proud Phuket's FAQ says 11:00, but its booking terms say 12:00, so ask at check-in. A late check-out depends on free rooms and often costs extra, so ask a few days before. Reception can usually keep your bags for the afternoon.

departure.title: Left luggage at the airport
departure.text: AIRPORTELs has a counter in the international terminal, on the ground floor (called '1st floor' in Thailand), at Exit 2 (Door 2). It is open 06:00-24:00 and costs 150 baht per bag for 24 hours (Oct 2026). Leave your bags there, then go to Nai Yang Beach, 5-10 minutes away.

departure.title: VAT refund: the shopping rules
departure.text: Buy in shops with the 'VAT Refund for Tourists' sign and spend at least 2,000 baht (with VAT) in one shop on one day. Show your passport and get the P.P.10 form and the original tax invoice; check that your name and passport number are right. You must fly out within 60 days. Hotels, food and services do not count.

departure.title: VAT refund at Phuket airport
departure.text: If your goods total 20,000 baht or more, show them with the forms at the Customs VAT counter before check-in. Keep in your hand luggage any watch, phone, laptop, bag or jewellery of 40,000 baht or more, and anything of 100,000 baht or more. After passport control, go to the VAT Refund Office (3rd floor). Up to 30,000 baht is paid in cash there.

departure.title: No departure card, and e-gates
departure.text: There is no departure card: the paper TM6 card has not been used at airports since July 2022, and the TDAC is only for entering Thailand. Since 13 June 2026, HKT has automatic passport gates for departures. You need an e-passport valid for 6 more months and must be at least 120 cm tall. Take off your hat, glasses and mask.

departure.title: Power banks and liquids
departure.text: Power banks go only in hand luggage, max 2 per person. Up to 100 Wh is fine, 100-160 Wh needs airline approval, and bigger or unlabelled ones are not allowed. Since June 2026 you may not use or charge them on the plane; keep them in the seat pocket or under the seat. Liquids: max 100 ml per bottle, in one clear 1-litre bag.

departure.title: No departure tax to pay
departure.text: The airport passenger fee is already in your ticket price: 1,120 baht for tickets issued from 20 June 2026 (730 baht before). You pay nothing extra at the airport.

departure.title: A relaxed last day near the airport
departure.text: Check out, then leave your bags at reception or at AIRPORTELs. Have lunch at Natural Restaurant or on Nai Yang Beach, then choose a massage with a free airport drop-off, plane spotting at Mai Khao (best until about 14:00) or the 13:30 tour at Soi Dog (open on Tuesday). Be at the terminal by 15:20.

departure.title: Paid lounges after passport control
departure.text: The Coral lounges are on the international side, after passport control. You can buy a pass online, for example a 2.5-hour pass for the Coral Executive Lounge on Klook. Priority Pass works only in some of them, so check before you go up.

solo.title: Social hostels in Patong
solo.text: Mad Monkey Phuket (Patong, 9.8 on Hostelworld) has a 'Meet Up' every evening at 19:00 with half-price beer, pub crawls on Tuesday and Thursday and a foam party on Saturday. Lub d Patong has pool party nights; Zostel Patong has daily pub crawls and pool parties. Dorm beds at Mad Monkey and Lub d: about 1,000-1,400 baht a night on 23-25 Jan.

solo.title: Hostelworld app chats
solo.text: Book a bed through Hostelworld, and the app opens chats with people in your hostel and in Phuket 7 days before check-in. 'Linkups' are meet-ups that hostels and travellers post, from dinners to nights out.

solo.title: Find the techno people
solo.text: Check Resident Advisor (Phuket page) and the Instagram pages of Shelter, Courage Bar, FAKE PALM and SUB: small parties are posted only 1-3 weeks ahead. Go early, stand near the booth and talk to the DJs and bar staff. They know the after-parties.

solo.title: Join-in boat trips
solo.text: Group boat tours are sold per person, so going alone costs the same. Examples: Khai Islands half day about 1,100 baht, James Bond Island 1,400-3,500, Phi Phi by speedboat 1,500-3,500. Pickup is often extra from Kamala or Nai Yang, and ask if the park fee is included. Book 1-2 days ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide.

solo.title: Drinks at parties
solo.text: Buy your own drinks and watch them being poured, or take closed cans and bottles. Never leave a drink alone, and never take pills or open drinks from strangers. Police raid parties and do urine tests, and drug use is a crime. If you suddenly feel very drunk or sick, tell security and call 1669.

solo.title: Plan the ride home
solo.text: Before you go out, check that Grab or Bolt works from the venue and keep at least 1,000 baht in cash for the ride, more for long rides. For Circoloco in Natai (Sat 23 Jan, until 03:00), book a driver for both ways. In Grab, use 'Share My Ride' so a friend can follow your car live.

solo.title: Phone, money and passport
solo.text: Clubs check your age (20+) with your passport, so carry it in a zip pocket and leave spare cards and most cash in the hotel safe. Take one card and some cash. Charge your phone, bring a small power bank and save your hotel in Google Maps offline.

solo.title: Share your location
solo.text: Before a night out, share your live location with a friend: Google Maps can share until you turn it off, and WhatsApp for up to 8 hours. Send the party name, your hotel and when you plan to be back. Message 'home safe' when you arrive.

solo.title: Help numbers
solo.text: Tourist Police 1155 (English, 24 hours), ambulance 1669, police 191. The Thailand Tourist Police app has an SOS button that sends your GPS position, and a live chat with officers in English. Install it before you go out.

solo.title: Budget for a room alone
solo.text: Most hotel rooms cost the same for one person as for two. For 23-26 Jan, expect about 400-1,800 baht for a dorm bed, 800-1,400 for a private room with a shared bathroom, and 2,100-3,600 for a room with your own bathroom or a mid-range hotel. Saturday 23 Jan is often the most expensive night.
